quote.translation: Since contingency carries the sense opposed to necessity, there should be three modes of contingency corresponding to the three modes of necessity, namely (1) categorical contingency, (2) hypothetical contingency and (3) disjunctive contingency.

regions.text: 偶然性を撕やうに三つの様態に區別することによつて初めて偶然性の意味が難多と統一とに於て明かになると思ふ。

quote.translation: It is only by distinguishing contingency into these three modes, I think, that its meaning becomes clear, both in its multiplicity and in its unity.

regions.text: 偶然に開する理論が常に明晰を絞くのは、問題そのものの困難にもよつてゐるのは勿論であるが、間題提出の出發點に於て、偶然性の様態の區分がなんら原理に基いて明晰に行はれず、その統一的把握が主題として明かに意識されないことに基くとこ事實としてこの三様態の皿分に相営するものはアリストテレスに見ることが出來る。

quote.translation: Theories of the contingent have always lacked clarity, and whilst this is partly due, of course, to the difficulty of the problem itself, much of it, I think, comes from the fact that, at the very point where the problem is posed, the modes of contingency have not been distinguished on any clear principle, and grasping them as a unity has not been consciously taken up as a theme.

quote.translation: As I shall discuss in detail later, Aristotle's symbebēkos (συμβεβηκός, accidens) corresponds to categorical contingency; automaton (αὐτόματον, casus) and tychē (τύχη, fortuna) correspond to hypothetical contingency; and endechomenon (ἐνδεχόμενον, contingens) corresponds to disjunctive contingency.
